headline: Hot US CPI and Fed talk of a 50bp December hike lift Treasuries 10bp, and KTBs fall twice as hard as the usual pass-through as foreigners dump futures into a second KOSPI rally day: the 10Y jumps 10.0bp to 3.950%, its biggest rise since Sep 28, and 2s3s un-inverts
summary: KTBs sold off across the curve in a bear move led by the belly: the 3Y rose 9.6bp to 3.729%, the 5Y 9.2bp to 3.810% and the 10Y 10.0bp to 3.950% (52nd percentile of its 1-year range), while the 30Y rose 5.6bp to 4.015% and the 50Y 5.0bp to 4.041%, so 10s30s flattened 4.4bp to 6.5bp and 3s10s held near its 1-year low at 22.1bp. The 2Y rose 8.5bp to 3.728%, lifting 2s3s back to +0.1bp, and the 10Y is now +9.7bp on the week and −5.8bp month to date. Bills were firm in yield: MSB 91-day rose 1.9bp to 3.193%, a 1-year high, CD held at 3.37% (also a 1-year high) and CP at 3.83%, so CP–CD stays 46bp (92nd percentile). Spread products barely moved against KTBs: KDB 3Y 25bp over (80th), AAA bank 1Y 40bp (88th, −2bp), AA- 3Y 68bp (72nd) and KEPCO 3Y 42.5bp (92nd).
drivers: US Treasuries: a 10bp sell-off, passed through at double the usual rate

US October CPI rose 0.4% m/m (f 0.3%) with core at 0.3% (f 0.2%), after Governor Waller said a core print near 0.3% could justify a 50bp December hike; a soft USD 42bn 10Y auction near 5.02% added to it. The US 10Y par yield rose 10bp to 4.98% and the 2Y about 18bp. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.47 that implied +4.7bp for the KTB 10Y against an actual +10.0bp, so about half the move was global and 5.3bp was local; the KTB–UST 10Y gap stayed at −103bp, the widest of the year. Treasuries are shut tonight for Veterans Day, so Thursday's open has little US input.
Foreign futures buying flips to selling

After four sessions of buying, foreigners sold 8,684 3Y and 4,469 10Y futures; brokers, banks and insurers absorbed it. The 3Y future fell 32 ticks to 103.51 and the 10Y 92 ticks to 108.56, both the largest falls in two months. Against our basket fair values of 103.64 and 108.61, the 3Y is 13 ticks cheap (9 ticks yesterday) and the 10Y 5 ticks cheap (1 tick rich yesterday), so futures led cash lower and the unwind of October's long may not be finished.

KOSPI rose 2.60% to 5,375.36 and KOSDAQ 5.6%, with foreigners net buyers of stock for a second day (about KRW 0.7–0.8tn); the won firmed 3.9 to 1,333.6, a two-week high. Exports for Nov 1–10 rose 111.9% y/y to a record USD 33.5bn, with chips up 331%, which strengthens the BOK's case for a November 26 hike to 3.25%.
Record fine for KTB primary dealers

The Fair Trade Commission fined 15 primary dealers a total of KRW 1.63tn for sharing bid rates in KTB auctions from 2020 to mid-2023 and referred seven for prosecution. Dealers said it chilled sentiment; the bigger question is whether PDs bid less aggressively at coming auctions, which would cheapen new issues at the margin.

view: Today was the test of the rotation trade: Treasuries rose 10bp and KTBs gave back 10bp, twice the usual 0.47 pass-through, because foreigners who had bought futures for four days sold into a second KOSPI rally day. Over four weeks the 10Y is still −23bp, of which −7bp is Treasuries at the weekly beta of 0.60 and −16bp is Korea's own rally, and the weekly rotation signal is +1.35 (daily +1.74), still in the bond-rally regime because KOSPI is −5% and margin credit −18% over four weeks. With a November 26 hike to 3.25% priced, the 2Y at 3.73% and CD at a 1-year high, I expect the 10Y to trade 3.85–4.05% into the BOK meeting; our 3.95% buy level filled at today's close and I keep it, stop 4.10%, target 3.80%. US PPI on Nov 13 and the 30Y auction on Nov 12 are the main risks at about 0.4–0.55bp per Treasury bp, and Treasuries are closed tonight, which gives the futures unwind a day to clear. I stay flat the 3s10s curve: the move was parallel, not a steepening, and the curve sits at its 1-year low. The rotation signal's record is better against Treasuries (hedged rally calls right 67% of the time and sell-off calls 69%, against 50% and 57% outright; Sharpe 1.29 vs 0.93, worst drawdown −26bp vs −36bp), so I hold the 10Y long against about 0.5 × US 10Y rather than outright, accepting the −103bp KTB–UST gap as the cost.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y rose 8.5bp to 3.728%, 83rd percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.38%), +12.7bp on the week; the 1Y is 3.613% (89th). 2s3s is back to +0.1bp (0th percentile, average 13bp) and 1s2s widened to 11.5bp (5th). MSB 91-day at 3.193% and CD at 3.37% are both 1-year highs and price a November 26 hike to 3.25%, which today's record exports support.
buckets.call: Close the fade-below-3.60% leg unfilled (now 13bp away). Keep: buy the 2Y above 3.80%, target 3.65%, stop 3.90%.

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s steepened only 0.4bp to 22.1bp (1st percentile, average 40bp) on a 10bp sell-off, so the bear move was parallel and gave no steepening. The 3s5s10s fly is −5.9bp (2nd percentile, average 4.4bp), so the 5Y is still rich to the wings. Our steepener from 29bp was stopped on Nov 5.
buckets.call: Stay flat. KOSPI has now rallied two days; re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures, DV01 about KRW 86k each side) only if it holds to Nov 17, target 30bp, stop 18bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.950% is at the 52nd percentile of a 3.20–4.60% range (average 3.91%). Our buy zone of 3.95–4.00% was reached at today's close, so the long is open at 3.95%. Half of today's +10bp was the US move at the 0.47 beta and half was local futures selling; the 10Y future closed 5 ticks below fair value.
buckets.call: Long from 3.95% (new), add at 4.00%, stop 4.10%, target 3.80%; prefer it against about 0.5 × US 10Y.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s narrowed 0.6bp to +2.6bp, 95th percentile (average −9.2bp), as the 50Y (+5.0bp) beat the 30Y (+5.6bp); the switch from +2.5bp is 0.1bp against. 20s30s inverted to −2.8bp, the deepest since June, with the 20Y lagging again (10s20s30s fly 12.1bp, 72nd). On Tuesday's trades 20-2 2050 was 3.9bp and 19-6 2039 3.7bp rich, while 25-8 2030 was 6.2bp cheap.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch from +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +6bp. Open, 0.1bp against.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The refreshed KDB fit (26 trades) puts the 3Y 24.9bp over KTB, 80th percentile (average 19bp), and revises yesterday to 24.7bp from 21.3bp, so the overweight from about 26bp is only 1bp in favour. The 1Y fit is 33.6bp over (89th) and KOFIA's 1Y KDB quote 27.9bp (72nd, average 23.6bp). KEXIM has only 3 trades (low confidence), so ignore its 38bp reading.
buckets.call: Hold from ~26bp; target 20bp, stop 28bp (3bp away). Open.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (34-trade fit) is 40.2bp over the 1Y KTB, 88th percentile (average 31bp), 2bp tighter as the KTB 1Y sold off; the 3Y is 37bp over (92nd). CD held at 3.37% and CP at 3.83%, so CP–CD is 46bp (92nd, average 28bp), while CD–MSB91 narrowed to 17.7bp (30th). IBK 1Y (18 trades) is 31bp over, 73rd percentile.
buckets.call: No change: prefer KDB over bank debentures; revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y rose 8.3bp to 4.410%, lagging the KTB 3Y, so the spread narrowed 1.3bp to 68bp (72nd percentile, average 61bp). KEPCO 3Y is 42.5bp over (92nd, average 34bp) and BBB- minus AA- 582bp (69th). Credit has not cheapened on the sell-off, and a second KOSPI rally day helps risk appetite.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI holds its rebound to Nov 17; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: US Treasuries closed for Veterans Day tonight (Nov 11), the US 30Y auction on Nov 12, US PPI on Nov 13, the college entrance exam on Nov 19 (KRX opens an hour late), Korea's Nov 1–20 exports around Nov 21–23, the BOK decision on Nov 26 (hike to 3.25% priced) and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; a hot PPI would hit KTBs at about 0.4–0.55bp per Treasury bp, and further foreign futures selling is the local risk.
